issues.legal_issue: A cess calculated by reference to the natural yield of a landholding classified as a distinct unit is a tax on land within the State legislature’s taxing competence.
material_facts: The amended levy applied annually to a tea estate treated as a separate unit and was calculated by reference to the quantity of green tea leaves produced there.
The green leaves were the natural yield of the tea estate, and the tea estate included land used for growing tea plants and land ancillary to their cultivation.
The challenge argued that the levy was really a tax on production because its amount varied with annual output and could be nil if leaves were not plucked.
issues.conclusion: The cess was a tax on land measured by its yield, not a tax on production, and was within the State legislature’s competence under Entry 49 of List II.
issues.legal_principle: Legislative entries are construed broadly, and the pith-and-substance doctrine identifies the true subject of a levy. The measure of a tax does not determine its character: a tax on land may be assessed by reference to its annual value, income, productivity, or yield. The Court applied Ralla Ram v. Province of East Punjab, Ajoy Kumar Mukherjee v. Local Board of Barpeta, Kunnathat Thathunni Moopil Nair v. State of Kerala, Assistant Commissioner v. Buckingham and Carnatic Co. Ltd., Federation of Hotel and Restaurant Association v. Union of India, and the distinction drawn in India Cement Ltd. v. State of Tamil Nadu and Orissa Cement Ltd. v. State of Orissa, where the levies were measured by royalty rather than the land’s yield. Entry 49 of List II is the relevant legislative head.

predicates.state_taxing_power_challenge: A constitutional challenge is made to a State levy on the ground that the State lacks legislative competence to impose it.
predicates.landholding_treated_as_tax_unit: The law treats a defined landholding as a distinct unit for imposing and assessing the levy.
predicates.levy_measured_by_natural_yield: The amount of the levy is calculated by reference to the natural produce or yield of that landholding.

issues.definition: When a State levy is challenged for lack of taxing competence, treating a landholding as a unit and measuring the levy by its natural yield means the levy falls within the State’s power to tax land.

issues.legal_issue: A discretionary exemption provision does not change a levy on land into a levy on another subject.
material_facts: The amended law empowered the State Government to exempt specified categories of tea estates producing below a stated quantity and located in specified areas.
The levy itself applied to tea estates as units and was measured by the quantity of green leaves produced.
issues.conclusion: The exemption power did not alter the character of the cess as a levy on land.
issues.legal_principle: The presence of an exemption provision, ordinarily included in taxing legislation for appropriate cases, does not by itself change the subject or character of the tax. The Court distinguished the earlier decision in Buxa Dooars Tea Co. Ltd. v. State of West Bengal because that levy was, in substance, imposed on tea despatches; it did not treat the exemption provision as independently determining the character of the levy.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_land_levy: A constitutional challenge concerns the character of a levy imposed in relation to land.
predicates.levy_attaches_to_land_unit: The levy is imposed on a defined landholding treated as a unit rather than on a transaction involving its produce.
predicates.government_has_discretionary_exemption_p: The government may exempt specified categories or cases from all or part of the levy.

issues.definition: A discretionary power to exempt categories or cases does not change the character of a levy that otherwise attaches to land as a unit.

issues.legal_issue: Central control of an industry and a central levy on its product do not displace State competence to tax the land on which the industry operates.
material_facts: The central legislation provided for control of the tea industry, including cultivation, and authorized a central excise cess on tea produced in India.
The State levy was imposed on land comprised in a tea estate and was measured by the estate’s green-leaf yield.
The Court treated the central excise levy and the State land cess as distinct in character and purpose.
issues.conclusion: The central legislation and central levy did not deprive the State legislature of competence to impose the land cess.
issues.legal_principle: Legislative competence depends on the true subject of the levy, not merely on the industry that ultimately bears its economic effect. A central levy on tea or tea leaves for the purposes of the central enactment is distinct from a State tax on land. The Court relied on the distinction between taxable subjects and aspects explained in Federation of Hotel and Restaurant Association v. Union of India, and considered the Tea Act, 1953, including Sections 2, 3(n), 10, 12–16, 16B–16D, and 25, alongside Entry 49 of List II and the relevant Union entries.

rule.if: challenge_to_state_land_levy and state_levy_is_on_land and central_law_controls_industry_or_product and central_levy_has_distinct_subject

predicates.challenge_to_state_land_levy: A constitutional challenge is made to a State levy imposed in relation to land used by an industry.
predicates.state_levy_is_on_land: The State levy is, in its true character, imposed on land rather than on the industry’s product or activity.
predicates.central_law_controls_industry_or_product: A central law regulates the relevant industry, its cultivation, or its product.
predicates.central_levy_has_distinct_subject: Any central levy concerns a taxable subject distinct from the land taxed by the State.

issues.definition: Central regulation of an industry or a distinct central levy on its product does not displace State taxing power when the State levy is in substance a tax on land.

issues.legal_issue: Applying a uniform levy to a class of landholdings is not discriminatory merely because the quality of their produce differs.
material_facts: The same method of levy applied to the tea estates in the relevant class, although the quality of tea produced by different estates could vary.
The petitioners did not establish hostile or unequal treatment resulting from that difference.
issues.conclusion: The uniform method of levy was not shown to be discriminatory.
issues.legal_principle: The burden rests on the person alleging discrimination to prove hostile unequal treatment, not merely a possible difference in outcomes. The Court applied the principle stated in Twyford Tea Co. Ltd. v. State of Kerala and Anr. and recognized that a legislature may use a uniform method inherent in a tax scheme.

rule.if: equality_challenge_to_tax and same_tax_method_applies_to_class and produce_quality_differs and not hostile_unequal_treatment_proved

predicates.equality_challenge_to_tax: A constitutional challenge alleges that a tax treats members of a class unequally.
predicates.same_tax_method_applies_to_class: The same method of taxation is applied to the relevant class of properties or taxpayers.
predicates.produce_quality_differs: The quality of produce varies among members of the taxed class.
predicates.hostile_unequal_treatment_proved: The challenger establishes hostile or unequal treatment among members of the class.

issues.definition: A uniform tax method is not shown to be discriminatory when produce quality differs but the challenger does not prove hostile unequal treatment.

issues.legal_issue: A retrospective validating amendment may impose a levy for a prior period when it remedies the defect that invalidated the earlier levy.
material_facts: An earlier levy had been invalidated because its substance was a levy on tea despatches rather than a levy on land.

The later amendment changed the basis of the levy to the production of green leaves on a tea estate treated as a land unit and gave the amended provisions retrospective effect for the period covered by the earlier levy.
The Court held that the defect identified in the earlier decision had been remedied.
issues.conclusion: The retrospective effect of the amended levy was valid.
issues.legal_principle: Where an amendment remedies the defect identified in an earlier decision, the legislature may give the corrected law retrospective effect to cover the period governed by the earlier enactment. The Court stated that a law valid in its substance may be valid prospectively and retrospectively, and relied on the established legislative practice of giving corrective amendments retrospective effect.

predicates.challenge_to_retroactive_tax: A constitutional challenge concerns a tax provision given effect for a period before its enactment.
predicates.amended_levy_cures_prior_defect: The amendment changes the levy so that it remedies the defect that invalidated the earlier version.
predicates.retroactivity_covers_period_of_prior_lev: The amendment applies the corrected levy to the period previously governed by the earlier levy.

issues.definition: A retrospective validating levy is valid when the amendment remedies the earlier defect and applies the corrected levy to the earlier period.
